name: moon-buggy
desc: Drive some car across the moon
why: A classic terminal driving game with a tiny, strange premise that still plays well and has lasted decades.

brief.what_it_is: Moon-buggy is a terminal game written in character graphics (ASCII art), where you drive a car across the moon's surface. Dangerous craters appear along the way, and you jump over them. You play from the keyboard in a curses-based terminal window, and the game keeps a high score table. Its input is keypresses and its output is text on screen.
brief.why_it_exists: Its author Jochen Voss wrote it as an ASCII homage to the 1982 arcade game Moon Patrol and the 1983 Commodore 64 clone of it. The homepage describes it as a simple character graphics game, and the project's voice is light and playful.
brief.how_it_works: The game is built on the curses library, so it runs in any terminal that curses (or the ncurses package) supports. The README notes that it does not work with BSD curses, so BSD systems need ncurses. Scores are kept in a score file whose location is set at build time, and the README says shared score files are supported.

commands_seen.context: Prints the version number; the README asks bug reports to include this output.
Generates the configure and INSTALL files when building from the git repository, not from a release tarball. Needs autoconf, automake and makeinfo.
The README's example configure line for GNU/Linux, placing the score file under /var/games and setting up setgid for shared scores.
Installs the program; the README says this step needs root permissions in its example.

brief.install_notes: Requires a curses library, with ncurses as the fallback; BSD curses will not work. Release tarballs ship with generated files, so they need only a C toolchain plus configure/make. Building from git needs GNU autoconf, automake and texinfo's makeinfo. The default install path is /usr/local/bin/moon-buggy, changeable with --prefix. The --with-setgid option makes the game setgid, which the README warns carries security risks. If curses is not auto-detected, use the --with-curses-includedir, --with-curses-header or --with-curses-libs options. Homebrew installation is not described in the README.
brief.standout: It is a faithful, text-only take on a Moon Patrol-style side-scroller that runs in any terminal, with a shared high score file and a title-screen key that shows the GPL licence. It has been around since at least 2000 and still gets releases.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the evidence shows. The download table on seehuhn.de lists version 1.1.0 as the stable release dated 2025-11-17, after older releases from 2006, 2004 and 2000. I did not check the git commit history, so recent commit activity is unverified.
brief.caveats: It needs a curses library and does not support BSD curses. The setgid install option is flagged in the README as a security risk. The README says there is no warranty, though it is GPL-licensed. The homepage also has a donation request. The homepage mentions an unofficial fan page, but I did not follow it.
quotes: Moon-buggy is a simple character graphics game, where you drive some kind of car across the moon's surface.
Unfortunately there are dangerous craters there. Fortunately your car can jump over them!
If you like my little game, you might consider buying me a present ;-)
